facts.text: Cape Elizabeth was renamed in 1615 by King Charles I after his sister Elizabeth of Bohemia, one of only four royal renamings that survived.
The first European settlement appeared on Richmond Island in 1628 when Walter Bagnall opened a trading post for rum and beaver pelts.
Fort Williams Park today houses the Cape Elizabeth Town Museum and the Fort Williams Museum, preserving the town’s military and maritime heritage.
Cape Elizabeth’s Portland Head Light, built in 1791, is the oldest lighthouse in Maine and a landmark that has guided ships for over two centuries.
Explorer Robert Peary, who claimed to reach the North Pole, grew up in Cape Elizabeth before setting out on his Arctic expeditions.
